title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: priority content for the Risky AI usage template
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap targets, licensing, policy controls and permissions are supported. The policy routes need small completeness corrections, and several background statements need additional Microsoft references; none changes the documented control or entitlement.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans priority content support for the Risky AI usage policy template in Insider Risk Management.
claims.quote: With this update, Risky AI usage policy template will support priority content.

claims.claim: Customers can define sensitive info types as priority content in the planned update.
claims.quote: Customers can define Sensitive Info Types (SITs), Trainable Classifiers, Sensitivity Labels as priority content

claims.claim: Customers can define trainable classifiers as priority content in the planned update.
claims.quote: Customers can define Sensitive Info Types (SITs), Trainable Classifiers, Sensitivity Labels as priority content

claims.quote: Customers can define Sensitive Info Types (SITs), Trainable Classifiers, Sensitivity Labels as priority content

claims.claim: The roadmap describes alerts only when activity matches the selected priority content.
claims.quote: and get alerted only when the activity matches the selected priority content.

claims.claim: No licence specific to priority content on the Risky AI usage template is published.

Product entitlements are stated; no separate priority-content licence is named.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no meter or charge specific to this priority-content setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management Risky AI usage priority content licensing billing meter price GCC GCC High DoD; read policies, configure, service description and purview-billing-models. Billing covers indicators and workloads, not a separate priority-content setting meter.

claims.claim: The supplied Purview policy-creation route reaches I want to prioritize content for a Risky AI usage policy.
claims.quote: On the Policy template page, choose a policy category and then select the template for the new policy. ... On the Content to prioritize page ... I want to prioritize content.
claims.fix: Keep controls[0].ui, which reaches the option. Append to its note: 'The workflow passes through Name and description, Admin units if shown, Users and groups, and Exclude users and groups (optional). To choose content, continue from I want to prioritize content to Sensitive info type > Add sensitive info type, Sensitivity labels > Add sensitivity label, or Trainable classifiers > Add trainable classifier.' These continuations are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-configure; the already-cited policies page confirms the Risky AI usage template supports priority content.

claims.claim: No documented PowerShell, Graph or other API sets priority content in this policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management priority content PowerShell Set policy sensitivity labels trainable classifiers scoring Graph API; Insider Risk Management PowerShell priority content New-InsiderRiskPolicy Set-InsiderRiskPolicy Microsoft Graph. Read configure and policies; no setting operation surfaced.

claims.claim: The supplied policy workflow reaches Scoring > Get alerts only for activity that includes priority content.
claims.quote: Scoring: Decide whether to assign risk scores to all risk management activities detected by this policy or only for activities that include priority content. Choose Get alerts for all activity or Get alerts only for activity that includes priority content.
claims.fix: Complete the workflow description in controls[1].note: 'The route is Microsoft Purview portal > Insider Risk Management > Policies > Create policy > Policy template > policy category > Risky AI usage > Name and description > Admin units (if shown) > Users and groups > Exclude users and groups (optional) > Content to prioritize > I want to prioritize content > Scoring > Get alerts only for activity that includes priority content. Before Scoring, complete the priority-content detail pages.' The omitted pages are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-configure; they do not change the template or control.

claims.claim: No documented automation call sets the policy's all-activity versus priority-only scoring choice.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management priority content PowerShell Set policy scoring Graph API; Insider Risk Management PowerShell priority content Get alerts only activity New-InsiderRiskPolicy Set-InsiderRiskPolicy Microsoft Graph. Read configure and policies; no scoring-setting operation surfaced.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Get alerts for all activity is the alternative scoring option and preserves scoring beyond priority content.
claims.quote: Decide whether to assign risk scores to all risk management activities detected by this policy or only for activities that include priority content. Choose Get alerts for all activity or Get alerts only for activity that includes priority content.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Cumulative exfiltration activity always receives a risk score even without priority content.
claims.quote: The option to only score activities containing priority content doesn't apply to cumulative exfiltration activities. Cumulative exfiltration activity always receives a risk score, regardless of whether or not it contains prioritized content.

claims.claim: Learn lists Risky AI usage among policy templates supporting priority-content selection.

claims.claim: Specifying priority content raises risk scores for associated activity.
claims.quote: Specifying content as a priority increases the risk score for any associated activity

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Priority content increases the chance of a high-severity alert.
claims.quote: Specifying content as a priority increases the risk score for any associated activity, which in turn increases the chance of generating a high severity alert.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Priority-only scoring leaves activity without priority content unscored, subject to the stated cumulative-exfiltration exception.
claims.quote: Risk scores are assigned and alerts are generated only when specified activities include priority content. Activities without priority content aren't scored

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Activities without priority content can still be reviewed if an alert is generated.
claims.quote: Activities without priority content aren't scored, but you can still review them if an alert is generated.

claims.claim: Some activities generate no alert unless related content contains a built-in or custom SIT or is specified as priority.
claims.quote: However, some activities don't generate an alert at all unless the related content contains built-in or custom sensitive info types or you specify it as a priority in the policy.

claims.claim: Configuring alerts only for priority content does not change risk score boosters.
claims.quote: If you configure a policy to generate alerts only for activity that includes priority content, no changes are applied to risk score boosters.
